results.claim: One planned FM2 mode investigates flame spread on the Moon in a normoxic environment, for example 34% oxygen at 0.558 atm.
results.quote: Mode 3: To investigate a planned normoxic environment (for example 34% O2 at 0.558 atm) on flame spread on the Moon compared to Earth.

results.claim: Saffire samples were also burned at 8.2 psia and 34% oxygen to simulate the atmosphere of deep space exploration vehicles.
results.quote: In addition, the samples were burned at 8.2 psia and 34% oxygen levels to simulate atmosphere conditions for deep space exploration vehicles.

results.claim: Local application of suppressant is not adequate to extinguish the flame: the local jet entrains air and sustains the flame even with the ambient airflow off.
results.quote: Also, current findings show that local application of suppressant is not adequate for flame extinguishment. The local jet entrains air and sustains the flame even when the ambient airflow is turned off.

results.claim: The 5 cm/s low-flow interval was used to cool the sample and ensure extinguishment when flow was stopped, avoiding the issues seen in Saffire IV-2.
results.quote: The primary purpose of this low-flow interval was to cool the sample material and ensure extinguishment upon flow termination, thereby avoiding the issues seen in SAFFIRE IV-2 [6].

results.claim: With the fan off for 70 seconds, the cotton flame grew back when flow resumed and burned another 150 seconds until the material was consumed.
results.quote: At approximately 280 seconds, the fan was turned off and remained off for 70 seconds. Despite this long interval, the flame grew back when the flow was turned on again and continued to burn for another 150 seconds until the material was consumed.

results.claim: On Saffire V-3, after an extended 300 second interval at reduced air flow (5 cm/s), the flame extinguished quickly when the flow was turned off.
results.quote: After an extended (300 second) interval at reduced air flow (5 cm/s), the flame extinguished quickly when the flow was turned off.

results.claim: Reduced air flow can extinguish faster than zero flow through convective cooling, but as a strategy it carries other risks given uncertain configurations and flow rates in a spacecraft.
results.quote: Furthermore, using reduced air flow rather than going to zero air flow can lead to more rapid extinction due to the convective cooling. However, as an extinguishment strategy, this would carry other risks given the uncertainty of configurations and flow rates in a spacecraft.

results.claim: Extinction cannot be assumed to occur quickly under quiescent conditions; thin materials, higher oxygen concentrations and heating of the solid fuel can all support extended burning.
results.quote: These results indicate that extinction of the fire cannot be assumed to occur quickly under quiescent conditions. Thin materials, higher oxygen concentrations and heating of the solid fuel can all support extended burning.

results.claim: For thin PMMA films the opposed-flow extinction velocities were about 1 cm/s for 100, 200 and 300 micrometer thickness and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 micrometers.
results.quote: When tests are repeated with samples of different thicknesses, the extinction velocities are found to be about 1 cm/s for 100, 200, and 300 μm and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 μm.

results.claim: At about 16 percent O2 the extinction velocities were about 2.6 cm/s (100 micrometer film) and about 4 cm/s (200 micrometer film); the report concludes the extinction velocity increases significantly as O2 is reduced and is independent of fuel thickness.
results.quote: Tests were also conducted at a lower O2 level of about 16 percent for two different thicknesses and the extinction velocities were found to be about 2.6 cm/s for 100 μm and about 4 cm/s for 200 μm. It should be mentioned that the width of the sample was different, 20 mm for the 100-μm sample and 10 mm for the 200-μm sample. Even though there is insufficient data at the lower O2 level, it is clear that the extinction velocity significantly increases as the O2 level is reduced and is independent of the fuel thickness.

results.claim: Sustained flame spread was not observed for opposed-flow velocities below approximately 4 mm/s for the 6.35 mm and 9.525 mm diameter black PMMA rods.
results.quote: Sustained flame spread for the conditions tested was not observed for opposed-flow velocities below approximately 4 mm/s for the 0.00635- and 0.009525-m- diameter rods.

results.claim: After extinction the hot PMMA can keep producing fuel for some time until it cools, and premixed flame oscillations along the rod persist much longer in microgravity than in normal gravity; the report says suppression efforts should be maintained until the burning material has cooled and stopped emitting vapors.
results.quote: After extinction, the hot material can continue to produce fuel for some time until it cools. Premixed flame oscillations along the rod have been observed for the concurrent rod geometry that persist much longer in microgravity than in normal gravity due to the lower rate of convective cooling of the rod. This suggests that spacecraft fire suppression efforts should be maintained until the burning material has cooled and stopped emitting vapors.

results.claim: The RTDFS tests run in BASS-II vindicated the theoretical and computational finding that the critical opposed-flow velocity for radiative extinction in microgravity is independent of fuel thickness.
results.quote: RTDFS vindicated the theoretical and computational findings that the critical opposed-flow velocity at which radiative extinction occurs in a microgravity environment is independent of fuel thickness

results.claim: After burning for about 7 minutes, the flame on the large fabric sample went out immediately when the air flow was shut off.
results.quote: The flame burned the entire allotted test time of about 7 min. at which point the air flow was shut off and the flame immediately extinguished

results.claim: For the SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric in concurrent flow, quenching speeds were between 1 and 5 cm/s, higher in lower-oxygen atmospheres.
results.quote: The quenching speeds were found to be between 1 and 5 cm/s with higher speed in lower oxygen atmosphere.

results.claim: Once the flame was blown downstream of the stagnation region it could not propagate back upstream at the low oxygen levels tested (16.1% O2 and lower); in the opposed-flow rod tests flame spread was not observed below 16.4% O2.
results.quote: so it seems that once the flame is blown downstream of the stagnation region, the flame is unable to propagate upstream for the low oxygen levels tested (16.1% O2 and lower). This is consistent with tests for opposed flow flame spread rods that were also done as part of BASS-II [18], where flame spread was not observed below 16.4 % O2.

results.claim: Thicker solids can store a great deal of heat even with only a small flame, and as a result extinction with the nitrogen jet was not possible for the given flow rate.
results.quote: Thicker solids can store a great deal of heat even with only a small flame. One result is that extinction with the nitrogen jet was not possible for the given flow rate.

results.claim: LUCI made the first extended-duration (longer than 25 seconds) combustion tests in simulated lunar gravity.
results.quote: These are the first-ever, extended-duration (greater than 25 seconds) combustion tests performed in simulated Lunar gravity.

results.claim: On 4-cm PMMA spheres, quenching at low velocity was seen as the flame tip shrinking upstream, and blowoff as a hole forming in the flame at the forward stagnation point.
results.quote: Quenching at low velocity is observed with the flame tip shrinking upstream and blowoff is observed when a hole forms in the flame at the forward flow stagnation point.

results.claim: GEL case 1 (quenching, sample inside the duct): at 4.83 cm/s flow the flame went out at 14.21% O2 and 1.04 atm.
GEL case 2 (blowoff, sample inside the duct): at 34.28 cm/s flow the flame blew off at 14.99% O2 and 1.06 atm.
At 50 cm/s the diffusion flame stabilized at the shoulder of the sphere after local stagnation-point blowoff, and as oxygen kept falling spinning flamelets formed.
results.quote: In the second case with a higher flow velocity (50 cm/s), the diffusion flame is stabilized at the shoulder of the spherical sample after local stagnation point blowoff. With steady decrease in ambient oxygen due to depletion, spinning flamelets are formed.

results.claim: On the two-sided PMMA sample, jets of fuel vapor from the bubbling surface kept the flame alive through a 15 second interval with no flow.
results.quote: These jets of fuel emerging from the surface provided sufficient mixing to keep the flame alive over the 15 second interval of no flow.

results.claim: On a PMMA sample (15-mm initial diameter, 17% O2/N2, 1 atm, flow under 1 cm/s) a nitrogen jet imposed near the end of the burn failed to extinguish the flame while the solid was very warm; the flame went out after flow reductions, when the flow speed was zero.
results.quote: Flow of less than 1 cm/s. Near the end of the burn, a jet of nitrogen is imposed but it fails to extinguish the flame. (Solid is very warm.) Finally after a series of flow reductions, the flame goes out when the flow speed is zero. Fuel: PMMA; 15-mm initial diameter; 17% O2/N2; 1 atm; Time between images: 1.3 sec

results.claim: Planned lunar surface missions will have crew cabins at 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) and 34% oxygen.
results.quote: Planned lunar surface missions will be at higher oxygen concentrations in the crew cabin (56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) and 34% oxygen)
